topic: Increase in Supreme Court Judge Strength

subtopics.title: CJI Appointment Convention and Collegium
subtopics.summary: Until 1973 the seniormost judge was normally appointed Chief Justice of India, a convention that was broken in 1973 and 1977. The Second Judges Case (1993) ruled that only the seniormost judge should be appointed CJI and that consultation means concurrence. The 2015 Fourth Judges Case struck down the NJAC and the 99th Amendment.
facts: Till 1973, the seniormost judge was normally appointed CJI
1973: AN Ray appointed CJI, superseding JM Shelat, KS Hegde and AN Grover
1977: MU Beg appointed CJI, superseding HR Khanna
1981 (First Judges Case): consultation only implies exchange of views
1993 (Second Judges Case): consultation changed to mean concurrence
1993: only the seniormost judge should be appointed CJI
1998 (Third Judges Case): CJI must consult a collegium of 4 seniormost judges
1998: if 2 judges give an adverse opinion, no recommendation is sent
2015 (Fourth Judges Case): 99th Amendment and NJAC Act declared void
NJAC: CJI chairperson, 2 seniormost judges, Law Minister, 2 eminent persons

subtopics.title: Jurisdiction and Temporary Appointments
subtopics.summary: The Supreme Court has appellate, original and advisory jurisdiction. Article 32 allows direct approach for violation of Fundamental Rights, while the President can seek an advisory opinion under Article 143 that is not binding. Articles 126, 127 and 128 allow an Acting CJI, ad hoc judges and retired judges in specified situations.
facts: Appellate jurisdiction covers appeals against lower court judgments
Appeals from High Courts need a certificate under Article 134A
Article 131 gives original jurisdiction in certain disputes
Article 32: direct approach for violation of Fundamental Rights
Article 143: President may seek advisory opinion on public importance questions
Advisory opinion is NOT binding on the President
Article 126: Acting CJI appointed when CJI post is vacant or absent
Article 127: CJI can appoint a High Court judge as ad hoc judge for lack of quorum
Article 127 needs prior consent of the President
Article 128: retired SC or HC judge can be requested to sit, with consent
